ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is voltage source US, marked with the upper end as positive and the lower end as negative. It is connected between the upper and lower two common rails, therefore the voltages of the upper and lower rails are determined by US. The middle branch has a current source, with the arrow downward and marked as IS, and resistor R2 connected in series below. In the right branch, the upper part is variable resistor RP, and the lower part is resistor R1 connected in series; the sliding contact of RP is indicated by the arrow on the right side, and is connected to the upper rail through the right-side wire. Reasoning: Since US>0, the voltage of the top rail relative to the bottom rail is US. In the right branch, the sliding contact of RP is connected to the top rail, so what truly participates in conducting in series with R1 is the effective resistance of the section of RP below the sliding contact. When the contact moves downward, the effective length of RP below the contact becomes shorter, therefore RP,eff decreases. Thus the total resistance of the right branch R1+RP,eff decreases, and under the fixed rail voltage US the current of the right branch increases. The current of the middle branch is fixed by the current source as IS, and does not change with the movement of the contact. Therefore the total current delivered from US increases. Because US is positive, the power delivered by the voltage source equals the positive voltage multiplied by the current it delivers, so the power delivered by US increases.

method.method_draft: First identify from the image the rail voltage imposed by U_S and the branch currents leaving the top rail. Treat the active part of R_P as the portion below the wiper because the wiper is connected to the top rail. When the contact moves downward, that active resistance decreases. Therefore the right-branch resistance R_1 + R_P,eff decreases and the right-branch current increases. The middle branch remains fixed at I_S. Hence the total current supplied by U_S increases, and with U_S positive the power emitted by U_S increases.

method.method_draft: View the circuit as a fixed-voltage two-terminal network powered by U_S. The middle branch has a fixed terminal current I_S, so its effect on the power balance does not change with the potentiometer motion. The right branch is the only part whose resistance changes; because the wiper is tied to the top rail, lowering the contact reduces the effective series resistance with R_1. At the fixed voltage U_S, the right branch absorbs more power. Therefore the voltage source must emit more power.
